hero.title: Can you swap to a cheaper car?
hero.p1: Compare keeping your financed vehicle with replacement options. The headline number is economic monthly cost — net ownership cost over your horizon, including exit equity — so a lower payment that loses value faster does not fool the math.
hero.p2: province-aware vehicle taxes (including BC PST-116 trade-in rules), EV rebates, multi-scenario trade-in ranges, terminal-equity TCO, field overrides, and a reverse max-budget solve for your target economic cost.

methodology.title: How the math works
methodology.p1: Everything runs in your browser; inputs never leave your device. Economic monthly cost is net horizon ownership cost divided by your ownership horizon. It includes opening equity, upfront cash, loan payments, operating costs, and subtracts estimated exit equity at the horizon.
methodology.p2: Auto loans use monthly compounding (APR ÷ periods per year), not Canadian mortgage semi-annual compounding. Vehicle taxes follow provincial rules; BC applies PST-116 (rate from full price, tax on net after trade-in). Rules last reviewed for {{rulesDate}}.
methodology.economicBody: Following AAA and Edmunds, depreciation is modeled as purchase value minus estimated resale at your ownership horizon — not as a separate monthly charge stacked on loan principal. Auto retained value uses an age-aware curve: new cars absorb the steep first-year drop; used cars (with an age field) start further down that curve, so more of today's purchase/market price is retained over the same horizon. Override retained % manually if you have a better estimate. Exit equity = exit value minus remaining loan balance. Economic monthly = (opening equity + upfront cash + loan payments through horizon + operating through horizon − exit equity) ÷ horizon months. Cash all-in monthly (loan + insurance + M&O + fuel) is shown separately as a liquidity view.
methodology.taxBody: For dealer purchases in BC, the PST rate is looked up from the full purchase price, then applied to purchase price minus trade-in. GST is 5% on the same net. Federal luxury tax (if any) uses the pre-tax price and is not reduced by trade-in. Private sales do not get a trade-in tax credit.
methodology.maxBody: Binary search finds the highest pre-tax purchase price whose economic monthly cost meets your target, accounting for taxes, rebates, trade equity, operating costs, loan amortization through the horizon, and exit equity.
methodology.disclaimer: Not financial or tax advice. Estimates for educational sensitivity analysis. Retained value is your assumption, not a Black Book or Edmunds forecast. Confirm with your dealer, lender, and provincial registry.
